Read the short guide for whichever side of the aisle you're on.

Planning a wedding or a big event means juggling a dozen vendors — venue, caterer, DJ, dhol, mehndi artist, photographer — across calls, texts and spreadsheets. Jorna brings it into one place: clients find vendors and compare complete teams; vendors show their packages, send contracts and keep track of every booking. Jorna doesn't hold anyone's money — clients pay vendors directly, on the schedule in their signed contract, and both sides keep track of each payment here.

Read the guide for your side:
For the host

Plan the whole thing in an afternoon

You bring the vision. Jorna helps you find the team, puts every booking in writing, and keeps the conversations and payments in one place.

Complete teamsThree vendor teams for your date and budget, side by side.
Agreed in writingEvery booking is a contract you've read and signed.
Pay vendors directlyOn the contract's schedule, with each payment recorded.

  1. Create your account

    Sign up with your email, or continue with Google. You only need your name, email and a password to start.

  2. Describe your celebration

    Tell Jorna where the event is, the date, how many guests, your budget and the vibe you're after. It takes about two minutes, and Jorna puts together three complete vendor teams — Budget, Balanced and Top Rated — to compare side by side.

    Don't love a pick? Swap any vendor for another who offers the same service.

  3. Or find vendors yourself

    Browse the marketplace by service, open a vendor's storefront to see their packages, photos and reviews, and ask them a question or send a request for your date.

  4. Review and sign the contract

    The vendor sends you a contract by email: what's included, the price, the payment schedule and their terms. Read it in full, and if something isn't right, ask for changes on the parts you'd like different — the vendor can accept, decline or revise.

    When it's right, sign it. We email you a one-time code to confirm it's you, and once the vendor countersigns, you're booked. Both of you get the signed PDF.

  5. Pay your vendor directly

    You pay the vendor yourself — Venmo or Zelle, as their contract says — on the dates in the payment schedule. After you've sent a payment, mark it as sent on your booking; the vendor confirms when it arrives. We'll remind you three days before a payment is due, and on the day.

    Good to know. Jorna never takes or holds your money. The contract is your record of what's owed and when.

  6. Stay in touch, and celebrate

    Message your vendors from your booking — details, timelines and questions stay in one thread. Need a different date? Request it from the booking, and the vendor answers there. Afterwards, leave a review to help the next host.

For the vendor

Show your work. Agree the terms. Keep track.

A storefront for your business, contracts clients sign online, and one place to see every booking, payment and conversation.

Be discoveredIn the marketplace and the teams clients compare.
Contracts, signed onlineSend a link; the client reviews, asks for changes and signs.
Paid directlyClients pay you; Jorna tracks what's due and what's arrived.

  1. Create your vendor account

    Sign up as a vendor, then set up in four short steps: what you offer (and your business name, if you go by one), where you work, how clients pay you, and your first package.

  2. List your packages

    Add each package with photos or video, and price it the way you actually charge: per event, per hour, per day or per guest. Add optional extras, and your own terms for each package.

    Why the unit matters. Jorna works out each booking's total from your rate and the client's details, so a per-guest price scales to their real guest count.

  3. Bring in inquiries

    Share your inquiry link — on Instagram, your website, anywhere — and requests from it land in Leads, with the date and guest count, and start a conversation in Messages you can answer right there. Clients make a free Jorna account to send one. Clients who find you on Jorna arrive there too.

  4. Send the contract

    Start from one of your templates: the package, any extras, the price, the payment schedule and your terms. Send it, and the client gets a link to review it. They can sign, or ask for changes you accept, decline or revise.

    Once they sign, countersign it — then it's a booking, and you both get the signed PDF.

  5. Get paid, directly

    Clients pay you straight to your Venmo or Zelle, on the contract's schedule. When a client marks a payment as sent, confirm it when it arrives; Jorna reminds clients before payments are due, and you can nudge one that's late.

    Good to know. Jorna doesn't process or hold payments, so nothing waits on us to reach you.

  6. Run your bookings

    Bookings shows what's at Deposit due, Upcoming and Done. Earnings tracks every payment, Calendar keeps your dates (sync it with Google so you're never double-booked), and Messages holds every conversation. On the day, check in at the venue so your client knows you've arrived.

How the money works

Agreed first, paid directly

Jorna doesn't take or hold anyone's money. The price and payment schedule are in the contract both sides sign; the client pays the vendor directly, and both keep track of each payment on the booking.
